name: Next.js frontend
description: Frontend web app on Next.js (App Router) and Tailwind, with data from external APIs (through thin, Zod-validated backend-for-frontend route handlers) or mocks, tested with Vitest and Playwright, delivered through GitHub Actions and Vercel. No database of its own.

specSections.title: Routes & Rendering Strategy
specSections.guidance: A table of every route: path, purpose, Server or Client Component at the top level, rendering mode (static, dynamic, or revalidated with an interval in seconds), the data it loads, whether it needs a signed-in user (if the consumed API has auth) and its loading, empty and error states. Say which parts are interactive client components and what is cached (fetch revalidate, cache tags) and for how long. Include the not-found and error pages.

specSections.title: Data Sources & Consumed APIs
specSections.guidance: For each external API or data source: base URL source (env var name), auth method (none, API key kept server-side, user token), and each endpoint used: method, path, request and response shape (fields and types, enough to write a Zod schema), rate limits and timeouts. State which calls go through a backend-for-frontend route under app/api (any call needing a secret, or needing response shaping) and which are fetched directly in Server Components. Map each upstream error (status or code) to the app's error code and the copy shown to the user. Describe the mock strategy: fixture data for tests (MSW handlers) and whether the app has a mock mode for local development.

specSections.title: Environment Variables
specSections.guidance: A table: name, public (NEXT_PUBLIC_) or server-only, environments (development, preview, production), source and which code uses it. Upstream API keys are server-only and read only in app/api route handlers or server-only modules; no server secret may carry the NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix. Write 'None' if the app needs none.

order.reason: Domain logic and helpers in lib/ come before the app/ steps that import them.

agents.name: Project scaffolder
agents.description: Bootstraps the Next.js + TypeScript + Tailwind skeleton: package.json, tooling config, root layout, Node pin and vercel.json. Owns tooling and configuration, not features.

agents.name: Domain logic engineer
agents.description: Implements the product's business rules and algorithms (filtering, sorting, pricing display, scoring, validation, state machines) as pure, deterministic, test-first TypeScript in lib/<domain>.

agents.name: API engineer (BFF)
agents.description: Builds backend-for-frontend route handlers under app/api and the lib/api helpers (upstream client, response schemas, error mapping), so secrets stay server-side and the UI gets validated, shaped data.

agents.name: UI engineer
agents.description: Builds App Router pages and Tailwind components: Server Components first, forms, loading/empty/error states, accessibility and mobile-first layout.

agents.name: Test engineer
agents.description: Writes Playwright end-to-end tests (primary journeys, upstream failure states, validation limits, mobile viewport) with mocked upstream APIs, and fills unit test gaps next to existing source.

agents.name: DevOps engineer
agents.description: Sets up GitHub Actions CI (checks + e2e), Dependabot and the PR template, vercel.json, and the environment variable inventory in .env.example. Makes the project safe to ship; never commits secrets.

checklist.item: Server-only secrets (upstream API keys, tokens) are read only in app/api route handlers or server-only modules; never in a "use client" file, a component or a NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable.
No secret is committed and no server-only secret carries the NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix.
BFF routes don't act as open proxies: the upstream host and paths are fixed in code, never taken from the request.
Untrusted upstream content is never rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitising.
Route handlers validate params, query and body with Zod before calling upstream.
Upstream responses are parsed with Zod schemas matching the spec's Data Sources & Consumed APIs section; unexpected shapes become a mapped error, not a crash.
Every error path returns a known error code through one error-code -> status map (lib/api/errors.ts), and upstream errors are mapped in one place.
Upstream calls have a timeout and handle network failure and rate limiting as specified.
Domain types in lib/types.ts are camelCase, derived from the Zod schemas, and the UI consumes only fields the schemas define.
Business rules live in pure, deterministic functions in lib/<domain> (no I/O, clock or randomness); routes and components call them instead of re-implementing them.
Rendering and caching follow the spec's Routes & Rendering Strategy (static, dynamic or revalidated per route); user-specific data is never statically cached.
Server Components are used for first render; client components are leaf-level and used only for interactivity and forms.
Route handlers stay thin (around 60 lines) and constants have one source of truth.
Every page has loading and error states (loading.tsx / error.tsx for data routes) plus empty and not-found states where they apply.
Upstream failures show the mapped error copy from one place (lib/ui/error-messages.ts) with a retry; forms keep input on failure and show field-level errors.
Pages work at 360px wide without horizontal scroll, tap targets are at least 44px, every control has a label and colour contrast meets WCAG AA.
CI runs typecheck, lint, test and build on every pull request, plus an e2e job.
Domain logic has tests citing spec IDs, covering every rule and worked example plus edge cases and a determinism test.
Each BFF route has tests for success, invalid input and a mapped upstream error, with the upstream mocked; no test calls a real external API.
E2E covers the primary journeys and at least one upstream failure state, against mocked upstreams.

protectedPaths.reason: Environment files hold secrets; only .env.example is committed.
